questions.cardText:
[Sociology] What was unique about Kowloon Walled City in Hong Kong?
A. It was the first centrally planned community
B. It was an area known for its exclusivity
C. It was the most densely populated area in the world
Answer: C. The Kowloon Walled City was once home to 33,000 residents crammed into just 6.4 acres. Originally a Chinese military fort, it became a lawless enclave with buildings constructed haphazardly up to 14 stories high. Despite the lack of government oversight, residents developed their own community organizations to manage daily life.
questions.de: Welche unregierte Enklave in Hongkong, ursprünglich ein chinesisches Militärfort, war 1987 mit rund 33.000 Bewohnern auf 2,6 Hektar einer der am dichtesten besiedelten Orte der Erde?
questions.en: Which ungoverned enclave in Hong Kong, originally a Chinese military fort, was by 1987 one of the most densely populated places on Earth, with about 33,000 residents on 2.6 hectares (6.4 acres)?

timeline.labelEn: Kowloon Walled City in Hong Kong is demolished (March 1993 to April 1994)
timeline.labelDe: Die Kowloon Walled City in Hongkong wird abgerissen (März 1993 bis April 1994)

questions.notes: Wikipedia confirms ~33,000 residents (1987) on 2.6 ha (6.4 acres) and a 13–14-storey height limit, but calls it 'one of the most densely populated places on Earth' rather than definitively the most; question asks the place, not the superlative.

questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] How many elements are listed in the periodic table, as of 2024?
A. 102  B. 118  C. 92
Answer: B.
questions.de: Wie viele chemische Elemente umfasst das Periodensystem (Stand 2024)?
questions.en: How many chemical elements are listed in the periodic table, as of 2024?

timeline.labelEn: IUPAC announces the names of elements 113, 115, 117 and 118, completing the seventh row of the periodic table
timeline.labelDe: Die IUPAC gibt die Namen der Elemente 113, 115, 117 und 118 bekannt und vervollständigt damit die siebte Periode des Periodensystems

questions.notes: All 118 were synthesised by 2010; the last four were named in 2016 (IUPAC announcement dated 30 November 2016, cited on the page). Still 118 as of 2024.
